text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The IMF board of directors has approved the second tranche of $80 million for Pakistan to be disbursed on Monday.

- The National Finance Commission is holding its crucial session in Quetta on Saturday to achieve a consensus on the distribution of resources between the centre and four provincial governments for the next five years.
- Saudi Arabia's anti-drug agents have seized 19 Pakistanis, including children as young as five, who tried to smuggle heroin concealed in private parts of their bodies, the newspaper Okaz reported.
- BBC World Service Television and Radio announced live coverage of elections in Pakistan.
- Pakistan's ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto said her government was toppled under a deep rooted cosnpiracy because she wanted to form an Islamic bloc.

- The caretaker government painted a very grim picture of the economy and concluded that without achieving 11.5 percent Gross Demostic Product growth, the future government would face an uphill task to put the economy back on rail.
- The Japanese government, the World Bank, and the Asian Development Bank have agreed to give loan of $785 million to recast Pakistan's National Drainage Programme at the Indus basin level.
- Over 61.44 percent of the total sugar production is lying with the sugar mills, sources said.
